results.summary_before: This project implements a custom system-on-chip using the SERV processor core under the RV32e instruction set. It provides GPIO inputs and outputs, a UART interface for serial communication, and SPI/QSPI interfaces for external flash and RAM memory. The design requires an external SPI Flash/RAM memory module, such as the QPMOD, and a USB-to-serial converter to interact with the system. It is notable for being a compact RISC-V SoC that fits within a 3x2 tile area and has been proven with external QSPI memory hardware.

results.summary_before: PolyWave is a mixed-signal four-channel waveform source with a digital engine driving four 16-bit R-2R DACs. The digital engine includes four 20-bit phase accumulators, a shared 16-bit LFSR noise source, a 4-bit sequencer, and DAC sample registers, and can run autonomously or accept direct byte writes. The analog outputs are on four pins, and the design uses the Tiny Tapeout custom GDS path with prebuilt layout files. Testing requires a clock/reset source, digital control signals, and an oscilloscope or logic analyzer to observe the outputs.

results.summary_before: This project is a small RISC-V microcontroller based on the PicoRV32 core, executing in place from an external SPI flash with 128 bytes of on-chip SRAM, a UART, and an 8-bit GPIO port. It requires an SPI flash (or an RP2040 emulating one) connected to the uio pins and a USB-serial adapter for the UART console. The design boots a program from flash and can run example firmware like a bouncing LED or a self-test that reports over UART. Notable features include the execute-in-place architecture to save area, closed timing at 50 MHz but tested at 25 MHz, and the need for external flash and serial hardware.

results.summary_before: The Kunal ML co-processor is a Verilog design that connects to an RP2040 over SPI to perform machine learning operations such as division and dot products. It uses Q8.8 signed fixed-point arithmetic and includes an SPI slave, an iterative 16-bit signed divider, and a command state machine with operand and weight registers. BUSY and DONE pins allow the host to poll operation status, though status can also be read via a READ_STAT command. No external components are required, and the design is notable for providing hardware acceleration for fixed-point ML primitives on a small ASIC.
